apex.label: Apex "Cold War" Era
apex.heading: 1987-1992: The Apex "Cold War"
apex.description: The band's first releases were defined by a "cold war" with their label, Apex Records, who suppressed their rock sound to push a marketable synth-pop image.

albums.title: Electric Color
albums.description: The Stardust Engine's forced mainstream debut, masking their true industrial rock tendencies under Apex Records' polished synth-pop veneer.

albums.title: Neon Hearts
albums.description: A continuation of the Apex Records "Cold War", featuring brighter synths but darker underlying lyrics hinting at the band's growing rebellion.

albums.title: Live in Chicago
albums.dspNotice: This simulated live environment violates commercial streaming metadata guidelines. It is available exclusively through the Engine Room Vault.
albums.description: A simulated live environment capturing the raw, unfiltered energy of the band right before the infamous Crash of '90.

albums.title: Friction
albums.description: The scrapped masterpiece. Apex Records deemed it too abrasive and aggressive, leading to the band's departure from the label.

freedom.label: The "Freedom" Era
freedom.heading: 1995-2001: The "Freedom" Era
freedom.description: After the contract was voided, the band retreated to "The Fortress"—a warehouse studio where they finally forged the industrial-rock sound they always heard in their heads.

albums.title: The Warehouse Tapes
albums.description: Forged in "The Fortress", this independent release finally unleashed the heavy, unfiltered industrial sound the band always intended to make.

albums.title: Ad Astra (Single)
albums.description: A soaring, atmospheric single that signaled a new era of experimental freedom for the band.

albums.title: Hard Reset
albums.description: A technological and thematic reset, blending aggressive guitars with cutting-edge 90s digital production.

albums.title: Forger Nation War Chest
albums.description: A heavy, political compilation dedicated to the loyal fans who stood by them during the label wars.

albums.title: Hard Reset Live
albums.dspNotice: This simulated live environment violates commercial streaming metadata guidelines. It is available exclusively through the Engine Room Vault.
albums.description: Recorded live on the 1998–1999 Hard Reset World Tour. Opens with the legendary continuous 3-song 'Stardust Suite' ('The Stardust Engine' -> 'Hard Reset' -> 'Brand New Scene') and closes with 'Electric Color'.

albums.title: Midnight Drivers
albums.description: A slick, nocturnal album infused with the anxiety and rapid technological shifts of the new millennium.

albums.title: Live at the Chancellery
albums.dspNotice: This simulated live environment violates commercial streaming metadata guidelines. It is available exclusively through the Engine Room Vault.
albums.description: Recorded live on August 24, 2002 at The Chancellery (University of the Piedmont, Charlottesville, VA) during the Midnight Drivers World Tour. Stages 'Electric Color' at Track 13 as a false ending before Ryan O'Connell formally introduces Crimson Node to close the night with 'The Flight Path (feat. Crimson Node)'.

err-planetarium.label: The Twin Moons & Progress Street
err-planetarium.heading: 2003-2005: The Twin Moons Project & Blacksburg Homecoming
err-planetarium.description: An ambitious dual-release planetarium project confronting the trauma of The Crash of '90, followed immediately by a nostalgic 2004 homecoming to Progress Street NE in Blacksburg and a triumphant farewell arena show in Norfolk before exhaustion forced the band into their Burnout Hiatus.

albums.title: Live in Virginia Beach
albums.dspNotice: This simulated live environment violates commercial streaming metadata guidelines. It is available exclusively through the Engine Room Vault.
albums.description: Recorded live on July 19, 2002 at the CTI Virginia Beach Amphitheater during the Midnight Drivers World Tour and released from the vault on February 18, 2003. Captures the first-ever recorded performance of 'The Flight Path', slipped unannounced into the middle of the set at Track 08 as a 5:14 mystery test run.

albums.title: Sanctuary (Zero-G)
albums.description: A zero-gravity atmospheric masterpiece showcasing the mathematically precise Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound. A sanctuary built on unwavering loyalty in the endless black.

albums.title: Mile Marker 98
albums.description: Blistering, distorted electric guitars and aggressive rock energy. A visceral, high-friction confrontation with the trauma of The Crash of '90.

albums.title: Progress Street
albums.description: Recorded at their home on Progress Street NE in Blacksburg, Virginia, this unapologetic 1980s AOR and stadium synth-rock love letter to their collegiate roots was the final studio album the band released before signing off to recharge during their Burnout Hiatus.

albums.title: Live in Norfolk
albums.dspNotice: This simulated live environment violates commercial streaming metadata guidelines. It is available exclusively through the Engine Room Vault.
albums.description: Recorded live in November 2004 under the geometric ribbed concrete dome of the Norfolk Scope Arena and released in March 2005. The final album The Stardust Engine put out before entering their ten-year Burnout Hiatus, featuring the live arena debuts of 'Sanctuary (Zero-G)', 'Mile Marker 98', and 'Progress Street'.

burnout-hiatus.label: The Burnout Hiatus
burnout-hiatus.heading: 2007-2011: The Burnout Hiatus & Archival Releases
burnout-hiatus.description: After releasing three full studio albums in under two years—culminating in 2004's Progress Street—exhaustion pushed the band into their "Burnout Hiatus" (2004-2014), yielding an archival vault compilation, an intimate acoustic studio retreat, and a 25th-anniversary Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ retrospective.

albums.title: Lost Sounds
albums.description: It collects the "Lost Gems" of the Apex era—polished demos, B-sides, and controversial tracks that the studio buried.

albums.title: Our Own Frequency
albums.description: An intimate exploration of the deep bond between Ryan and Cassidy as they peel back their rock-star personas.

albums.title: Starfield Calibration
albums.genre: 80s Cosmic Pop / Atmospheric Synth-Pop / Space Rock
albums.description: Released on October 18, 2011 during the Burnout Hiatus to celebrate the exact 25th Anniversary of 'Ignition (The Forger's Call)' debuting inside The Crucible on October 18, 1986, this 14-track retrospective reimagines foundational Stardust Engine classics (1987–2001) entirely within Cassidy O'Connell's zero-gravity Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™.

reignition.label: The Reignition Era
reignition.heading: 2014-Present: The Reignition Era & 30th Anniversary Homecoming
reignition.description: Returning from their ten-year Burnout Hiatus with renewed creative fire, The Stardust Engine launched their global Reignition return and brought the tour home to Blacksburg on May 21, 2016 inside The Crucible with all 300 members of the CPI Marching Forgers.

albums.title: Reignition
albums.dspNotice: In studio production — Complete 11-track 1980s AOR and Cosmic Synth-Pop comeback album setting the stage for 2016's Live at the Crucible.
albums.genre: 1980s AOR / Melodic Stadium Rock / 80s Cosmic Synth-Pop
albums.description: Ten years after exhaustion forced the family to turn off the studio switches on 2004's Progress Street ('Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street'), The Stardust Engine returns rested, recharged, and ready to perform again. Released in October 2015 immediately following Holly O'Connell's August 2015 Delaware Migration and CPI's 52–0 Norfolk Reckoning, Reignition ends the decade-long Burnout Hiatus and sets the stage for 2016's Live at the Crucible.

albums.title: Live at the Crucible
albums.dspNotice: Recorded live inside The Crucible on May 21, 2016 with the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers. Full multi-disc live album in production following the studio release of 2015's Reignition; the Grand Finale Encore ('Electric Color (Live at the Crucible)') is available for immediate streaming in The Listening Room and RaggieSoft Book Reader.
albums.genre: Live Stadium Rock / 1980s AOR / Collegiate Marching Band Rock
albums.description: Recorded live on Saturday, May 21, 2016 inside The Crucible in Blacksburg, Virginia—Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute's 65,000-seat stadium—celebrating the 30th Anniversary of 1986's 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' with the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers and closing with a secret 5:26 1980s AOR Stadium Rock reclamation of 'Electric Color'.
